observations.explanation: The paper describes retrieval on demand and evaluation of passage relevance, segment support, and usefulness (PDF pp. 1, 4). These mechanisms distinguish the method from indiscriminately supplying fixed passages.

The ASQA table reports citation precision and recall of 70.3 and 71.3 for SELF-RAG 13B (PDF p. 8). The paper says its ASQA precision and recall exceed those of all models except ChatGPT, and the listed retrieval baselines are generally lower on these metrics (PDF p. 8). “Most listed baselines” is appropriately qualified.

The ablation reports drops from the SELF-RAG baseline when using only the top passage on PopQA and ASQA, and when removing ISSUP scoring on ASQA (PDF p. 9). The results support the stated contribution of retrieval selection and support-based scoring, with the claim limited to particular tasks.

The human evaluation sampled 50 PopQA and biography examples, and reports that relevance and support judgments were mostly aligned with annotators (PDF p. 10). The paper’s ethical concerns explicitly state that outputs may still not be fully supported by citations (PDF p. 11). The observation carefully notes that the small evaluation does not establish broader reliability.
